ADDICTION MEDICINE NOTE   Date: 2025-11-28
59F, ambulatory follow-up visit in the outpatient program.

S:
Patient returns for scheduled follow-up in the outpatient program. She reports that cravings remain present most evenings but are less intense than last month. She attends group twice weekly and individual counseling on Wednesdays. She works as a hotel housekeeper and finds the physical demands tiring. She could not complete 7 of her scheduled shifts last month because of symptoms. Denies chest pain. Sleep is broken, averaging about 5 hours. Appetite is fair; diet is high in sugary drinks, which was discussed. Lives with her sister, who supports her treatment and drives her to appointments.

O:
BP 126/80, HR 82, RR 14, Temp 98.4 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 158 lb, stable.
General: alert, cooperative, tired appearing.
HEENT: pupils equal and reactive.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Skin: no track marks or lesions.
Psych: linear thought process, fair insight, engaged in goal setting.
Labs (last week): Hgb 11.5 g/dL, A1c 6.0%, comprehensive metabolic panel within normal limits. Urine drug screen reviewed with patient.

A/P:
1. Psychoactive substance dependence, active, engaged in outpatient treatment. Continue group and individual counseling and current medication-assisted treatment. Reviewed a relapse-prevention plan and evening coping strategies. Provided crisis line information and confirmed the next session.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding short daily walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
3. Anemia, stable on recheck. Continue oral iron daily with vitamin C. Repeat CBC in 3 months.
4. Function and work: symptoms are affecting her ability to keep regular shifts. Discussed documentation to support a gradual return to a steady schedule.

Return to the program in 2 weeks, sooner if cravings escalate.
